main:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Reads n decimal strings, converts each into a fixed-point scaled long long value, rejects values with a nonzero remainder modulo 100000, enumerates the divisors of 100000000, and for each valid value counts previous valid values at the lower-bound divisor index before updating divisor counts, printing the final total." main]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Read a long long integer n from standard input using scanf("%lld", &n). RESULT n]
            [COMMAND In the outer loop for i from 0 to n-1, read a whitespace-delimited string token into char buffer s, set a[i] = 0, and set k = 0. RESULT a]
            [COMMAND For the current string s, for each character index j from 0 while s[j] != '\0': if s[j] is not '.', update a[i] = 10 * a[i] + (s[j] - '0'), and if k > 0 then increment k; if s[j] is '.', set k = 1. RESULT a]
            [COMMAND After scanning each string, if k == 0 then set k = 1. Then while k < 10, multiply a[i] by 10 and increment k. This scales the digit value by 10^(9 - fractional_digit_count) for values with no more than 9 fractional digits; exactly 9 fractional digits causes no extra scaling, and more than 9 fractional digits also causes no scaling. RESULT a]
            [COMMAND Set q = 100000. For i from 0 to n-1, if a[i] % q > 0 then set a[i] = -1; otherwise set a[i] = a[i] / q. RESULT a]
            [COMMAND Set q = 100000000 and j = 0. For i from 1 while i * i <= q, if q % i == 0 then store b[j] = i and increment j. RESULT b]
            [COMMAND After the ascending divisor loop, decrement i once; if i * i == q then decrement i once more. Then for i while i > 0, if q % i == 0 then store b[j] = q / i and increment j, thus completing the sorted ascending list b of all divisors of 100000000. RESULT b]
            [COMMAND For i from 0 to j-1, set c[i] = 0. Set ans = 0. RESULT c]
            [COMMAND For i from 0 to n-1, if a[i] < 0 then skip the remaining statements for this iteration and continue with the next i. RESULT none]
            [COMMAND For a valid a[i], compute l = q / gcd(q, a[i]). RESULT l]
            [COMMAND Set min = -1 and max = j. While max - min > 1, compute mid = (max + min) / 2; if b[mid] < l then set min = mid, otherwise set max = mid. After the loop, max is the first index in b with b[max] >= l, or max == j if no such index exists. RESULT max]
            [COMMAND Before updating c for the current value, add c[max] to ans. RESULT ans]
            [COMMAND For k from 0 to j-1, if a[i] % b[k] == 0 then increment c[k]. RESULT c]
            [COMMAND Print ans as a long long integer followed by a newline using printf("%lld\n", ans). RESULT stdout]
            [COMMAND Return 0 from main. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
